audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows contradicted the content prose. Level 1 read Skill while whys[0], spikes[0] and early all say it is Maokai's outright; Level 2 read Jax while whys[1] says the trade is even; 4-5 and 6 read Skill while whys[3] and whys[4] describe Jax owning both; first item read Jax while whys[5] describes it levelling off; 2+ items read Jax while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Maokai reclaims it.
audit.why: The lane has a very clear shape — Maokai's level 1 before Counter Strike exists, Jax's from 3 through 6, Maokai's again once he is a full tank who declines the duel — and only the tokens failed to say so. The mirror audit set rows 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 to exactly this and noted row 2 already agreed.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Maokai / Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill / Maokai as one atomic group of matched full+content pairs, with ratings moved to 7/5/5/3/3/5/7. whys[5] rewritten so the first-item row genuinely reads as even.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phase whys were boilerplate; none named a spike or carried a number.
audit.why: Every stage here has a concrete trigger: Counter Strike not existing at 1, Empower's 300 range at 2, the three-ability combo at 3, Counter Strike falling to 11s at 4-5, Grandmaster-at-Arms on 110s at 6, and Heartsteel at first item.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten with those triggers and figures.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5] all describe Counter Strike as 'Dodges autos + stuns' with no cooldown and, crucially, without saying what it does NOT dodge. Riot's text: he 'dodges all incoming ATTACKS for a short duration'. Abilities are not attacks.
audit.why: It changes what you do inside the dodge window. Bramble Smash and Sapling Toss damage land through Counter Strike in full — only the autos are lost. A Maokai who thinks the whole window is dead time stands still for it instead of casting through it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with 17s at rank 1, the 300 range, and the attacks-only distinction spelled out. The mirror audit made the same correction on its side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said Twisted Advance is a lock-on dash Jax cannot avoid.
audit.why: Counter Strike is an attack-dodge, not an evasion, so it does nothing against a targeted dash — the root always lands. The page frames the whole matchup around fearing Counter Strike and never says which of your tools it cannot touch.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeGood, together with the instruction to Q him out of Empower's 300 range.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Jax contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Counter Strike does not exist yet, so a sapling and a Bramble Smash chunk him with nothing to dodge them.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Jax's Counter Strike is down.
edits.after: Even at 2: Empower is only 300 range and 7s, and Sap Magic heals the chip. Take short trades, refuse the extended one.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jax must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His level: with all three up he baits your W, holds Counter Strike through the rooted auto, then recasts to stun. Do not open.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His stretch: Counter Strike falls toward 11s while your W sits at 11s and does far less. Farm, shove with saplings, give nothing.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jax's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms on 110s adds armour, MR and third-strike magic damage — his cleanest all-in. Root to disengage, not to duel.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Counter Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: It levels off: Heartsteel HP blunts his burst but his on-hit still wins a straight duel.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Jax carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on it swings back — but only if you decline the duel. Sapling the wave, W to peel, and fight where five people are.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1, 300 range, and it dodges ATTACKS only. Bramble Smash and saplings land through it. - Leap Strike: 8s, 700 range. - Grandmaster-at-Arms: 110s.

edits.before: W-root Jax the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: Twisted Advance locks on — he cannot dodge it. Root him once Counter Strike is spent, Q him out of his 300-range Empower.

edits.before: Your first tank item starts blunting his burst and Sap Magic holds, but his Trinity/on-hit spike still edges a half-built you — root to disengage, not to duel.
edits.after: It levels off: my first tank item blunts his burst and Sap Magic holds, while his Trinity/on-hit spike matches it — root to disengage, not to duel, and neither owns the window.

notes: packet.defects claims three wrong ability names — 'Land Twisted Advance', 'Use Sapling Toss' and "Nature's Grasp's". All three are FALSE POSITIVES: correct Maokai names with a leading verb or a trailing possessive, which is what the matcher scored. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion on the two it saw. The content layer for this matchup is the strongest I have seen on this champion — real names, real sequencing, the Counter-Strike-through-the-rooted-auto trick spelled out — and the entire defect was that the full layer and the chart tokens never caught up with it.
